question.prompt: Suppose that \(P = 2^m\) and \(Q = 3^n.\) Which of the following is equal to \(12^{mn}\) for every pair of integers \((m, n)?\)

solutions.explanation:
Since \(P\) and \(Q\) are powers of 2 and 3, rewrite \(12=2^2\cdot3\) using those same bases. The power-of-a-product and power-of-a-power rules give
\[
\begin{aligned}
12^{mn}
&=(2^2\cdot3)^{mn}\\
&=2^{2mn}3^{mn}\\
&=(2^m)^{2n}(3^n)^m\\
&=P^{2n}Q^m.
\end{aligned}
\]
All bases involved are positive, so these rules remain valid when either integer exponent is zero or negative. Thus the expression is \(P^{2n}Q^m\), choice E.
solutions.title: Rewrite using bases 2 and 3
